To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reticulocytes of the chicken and the duck, which are the only two avian species that have been examined, are capable of producing a protein that is similar to the mammalian haemoglobin beta chain.

the reticulocytes of chickens are capable of synthesizing a protein that is similar in size and function to mammalian serum transferrin, but that this synthesis can be inhibited by the presence of a specific inhibitor in the diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the mechanisms by means of which haem regulates the initiation of protein synthetase in the mammalian cell-free system, reticulocyte ly-sate, and with the elucidation in this system of the mechanism by which the availability of haem controls the initiation of protein synthe-sis.

the elucidation of the mechanisms by means of which the rate of protein biosynthesis is regulated in mammalian cells, and with the elucidation and exploitation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the initiation of protein biosynthesis in mammalian cells and cell-free systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the reticucocyte lysate, the rate of initiation is controlled by a combination of the availability of haem, the concentration of haem-regulated inhibitor (HRI), the concentration of haemin, the availability of aminoacyl-tRNAs and the availability of GTP and ATP.

the reticulocytes lysate is a highly specialised translation system, in which the initiation of translation is controlled by a single mechanism, which operates at the level of the availability of the initiation factor eIF-2 and its guanylyl transferase activity.
the reticulocytelysate is a complex and highly regulated system, the components and mechanisms of which are still incompletely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reticulocytes are not a good model system for studying the control of protein biosynthesis in the intact cell.

the initiation of protein is controlled in the reticu- locyte by the availability of haem and that this control is exerted through the action of the haem-regulated eukaryotic initiation factor 2 (eIF-2) and a haem-regulated protein kinase (HRI).

the initiation of protein-synthesis in the reticu­ locyte lysate is controlled by the availability of haem, which regulates the synthesis of a haem-regulated inhibitor of protein synthesis, and by the presence or absence of the haem-regulated in­ hibitor of protein synthesis, which regulates the activity of the initiation factor eIF-2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reticulocytes are a great model system for studying the regulation of protein synthesis.
there are a lot of different ways to control the initiation of protein translation.
the reticulocytes have an amazing ability to sense the environment and respond accordingly.
